messages:
jules: spotted ACCESS_KEY_ID pattern in an image from our eu-builder pipeline. likely baked into the artifact. tagging @maya @leo.

maya: thanks. can you paste the registry path and digest? i'll rotate keys ASAP.

jules: eu.registry/agent-builder@sha256:bee9f3. log path in image=/var/build/logs/ci.log. build user=agent-builder.

leo: i'll quarantine the image and add a registry policy to block that digest. also adding a CI check to remove /var/build/logs.

rita: running quick cluster scan for that digest and searching for the pattern in other images.

oncall-sre: i'm online. i'll coordinate key deactivation and CloudTrail watch.

maya: workflow: 1) aws iam list-access-keys --user-name agent-builder 2) aws iam update-access-key --access-key-id <id> --status Inactive 3) create new key and store in Vault at secret/data/ci/agent-builder 4) rewrap any transit ciphertexts if necessary.

sec-bot: secret-scan alert: 'ACCESS_KEY_ID' pattern matched in image sha256:bee9f3. incident SEC-5010 opened.

leo: blocked digest and tagged as quarantined. pushed pipeline change to fail builds that include /var/build/logs.

rita: scan found two staging images with same pattern; quarantined. no running containers expose the file.

oncall-sre: revoked keys at 4123456800, no successful API calls detected. monitoring CloudTrail for anomalies.

maya: rotation done, new creds in Vault. rebuilt image without logs and pushed new digest sha256:ccd0aa.

jules: thanks team. postmortem assigned to me. checklist: CI sanitization (leo), Vault audit retention bump (maya), org note on ephemeral creds (rita). i'll post follow-up tomorrow.

sec-bot: SEC-5010 status -> contained. monitoring enabled.
